paragraphs.en: THE BROTHERS GRIMM FAIRY TALES
paragraphs.zh: 《格林兄弟童话》

paragraphs.en: THE GOLDEN BIRD
paragraphs.zh: 金鸟

paragraphs.en: A certain king had a beautiful garden, and in the garden stood a tree which bore golden apples. These apples were always counted, and about the time when they began to grow ripe it was found that every night one of them was gone. The king became very angry at this, and ordered the gardener to keep watch all night under the tree. The gardener set his eldest son to watch; but about twelve o’clock he fell asleep, and in the morning another of the apples was missing. Then the second son was ordered to watch; and at midnight he too fell asleep, and in the morning another apple was gone. Then the third son offered to keep watch; but the gardener at first would not let him, for fear some harm should come to him: however, at last he consented, and the young man laid himself under the tree to watch. As the clock struck twelve he heard a rustling noise in the air, and a bird came flying that was of pure gold; and as it was snapping at one of the apples with its beak, the gardener’s son jumped up and shot an arrow at it. But the arrow did the bird no harm; only it dropped a golden feather from its tail, and then flew away. The golden feather was brought to the king in the morning, and all the council was called together. Everyone agreed that it was worth more than all the wealth of the kingdom: but the king said, ‘One feather is of no use to me, I must have the whole bird.’
paragraphs.zh: 有一位国王有一个美丽的花园，花园里有一棵结金苹果的树。这些苹果总是被数着，每当它们开始成熟的时候，人们发现每天晚上都会有一个苹果不见了。国王对此非常生气，命令园丁整夜在树下守着。园丁让他的大儿子去守夜；但到了半夜十二点，他便睡着了，第二天早上，又有一个苹果不见了。于是，国王又命令第二个儿子去守夜；到了半夜，他也睡着了，第二天早上，又有一个苹果不见了。 三儿子主动提出守夜，但园丁起初不肯让他去，担心他会受到伤害；然而最后他还是同意了，年轻人于是躺在树下守夜。当钟声敲响十二下时，他听到空中有沙沙的响动，一只纯金的鸟飞了过来；当它用嘴啄食其中一个苹果时，园丁的儿子跳起来朝它射出一支箭。但箭并没有伤害到那只鸟，只是它从尾巴上掉下了一根金羽毛，然后飞走了。第二天早上，那根金羽毛被带到了国王面前，所有人都…… 理事会召开了。每个人都认为它比王国的所有财富都更有价值；但国王说：“一根羽毛对我来说毫无用处，我想要整个鸟。”

paragraphs.en: Then the gardener’s eldest son set out and thought to find the golden bird very easily; and when he had gone but a little way, he came to a wood, and by the side of the wood he saw a fox sitting; so he took his bow and made ready to shoot at it. Then the fox said, ‘Do not shoot me, for I will give you good counsel; I know what your business is, and that you want to find the golden bird. You will reach a village in the evening; and when you get there, you will see two inns opposite to each other, one of which is very pleasant and beautiful to look at: go not in there, but rest for the night in the other, though it may appear to you to be very poor and mean.’ But the son thought to himself, ‘What can such a beast as this know about the matter?’ So he shot his arrow at the fox; but he missed it, and it set up its tail above its back and ran into the wood. Then he went his way, and in the evening came to the village where the two inns were; and in one of these were people singing, and dancing, and feasting; but the other looked very dirty, and poor. ‘I should be very silly,’ said he, ‘if I went to that shabby house, and left this charming place’; so he went into the smart house, and ate and drank at his ease, and forgot the bird, and his country too.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，园丁的大儿子出发了，他以为要找到金鸟会很容易；他刚走了一小段路，就来到一片树林，树林边坐着一只狐狸；于是他拿起弓，准备射向它。狐狸说：“别射我，我会给你好的建议；我知道你的目的，你想要找到金鸟。你将在傍晚到达一个村庄；当你到了那里，会看到两家相对的旅馆，其中一家看起来非常舒适漂亮：不要进去，而在那家旅馆过夜。 另一个看起来虽然在你眼中可能很贫穷卑微。’但儿子心里想：‘这种野兽能懂什么？’于是他朝狐狸射出箭，但射偏了，狐狸竖起尾巴，背朝上跑进了树林。接着他继续前行，傍晚时分来到了那两个旅馆所在的村庄；其中一家屋里有人在唱歌、跳舞、宴饮；而另一家却看起来非常肮脏、贫穷。‘如果我跑去那破房子，而舍弃这个迷人的地方，那我可真是傻瓜，’他说着，于是走进了那家体面的旅馆， 他随意地吃喝，忘记了那只鸟，也忘记了祖国。

paragraphs.en: Time passed on; and as the eldest son did not come back, and no tidings were heard of him, the second son set out, and the same thing happened to him. He met the fox, who gave him the good advice: but when he came to the two inns, his eldest brother was standing at the window where the merrymaking was, and called to him to come in; and he could not withstand the temptation, but went in, and forgot the golden bird and his country in the same manner.
paragraphs.zh: 时间过去了；由于长子没有回来，也没有他的消息，次子便出发了，同样的事情也发生在了他的身上。他遇到了狐狸，狐狸给了他好的建议；但当他来到那两家客栈时，他的长兄正站在有欢宴的窗户旁，叫他进去；他无法抗拒诱惑，便进去了，同样忘记了金鸟和自己的祖国。

paragraphs.en: Time passed on again, and the youngest son too wished to set out into the wide world to seek for the golden bird; but his father would not listen to it for a long while, for he was very fond of his son, and was afraid that some ill luck might happen to him also, and prevent his coming back. However, at last it was agreed he should go, for he would not rest at home; and as he came to the wood, he met the fox, and heard the same good counsel. But he was thankful to the fox, and did not attempt his life as his brothers had done; so the fox said, ‘Sit upon my tail, and you will travel faster.’ So he sat down, and the fox began to run, and away they went over stock and stone so quick that their hair whistled in the wind.
paragraphs.zh: 时间又过去了，最小的儿子也想出发到广阔的世界中去寻找金鸟；但他的父亲很久都不愿听从，因为他非常疼爱自己的儿子，担心他也会遇到不幸，无法回来。然而，最后还是同意他去了，因为儿子在家里坐立不安；当他来到树林时，遇到了狐狸，也听到了同样的忠告。但他感谢狐狸，并没有像他的兄弟们那样企图杀害它；于是狐狸说：“坐在我尾巴上，你就能更快地旅行。”所以 他坐了下来，狐狸开始奔跑，他们迅速地翻过树桩和石头，快得连头发都在风中呼呼作响。

paragraphs.en: When they came to the village, the son followed the fox’s counsel, and without looking about him went to the shabby inn and rested there all night at his ease. In the morning came the fox again and met him as he was beginning his journey, and said, ‘Go straight forward, till you come to a castle, before which lie a whole troop of soldiers fast asleep and snoring: take no notice of them, but go into the castle and pass on and on till you come to a room, where the golden bird sits in a wooden cage; close by it stands a beautiful golden cage; but do not try to take the bird out of the shabby cage and put it into the handsome one, otherwise you will repent it.’ Then the fox stretched out his tail again, and the young man sat himself down, and away they went over stock and stone till their hair whistled in the wind.
paragraphs.zh: 当他们来到村庄时，儿子听从了狐狸的建议，没有四下张望，就直接去了那家破旧的旅馆，整晚安安稳稳地休息。第二天早上，狐狸再次出现，这时正逢他准备启程，狐狸说：“继续往前走，直到你来到一座城堡，城堡前有一队士兵正睡得鼾声如雷：不要理会他们，直接走进城堡，一直往前走，直到来到一间房间，那里有一只金鸟关在木制的笼子里；旁边还有一个漂亮的金笼子；但不要试图把鸟从那个破旧的笼子里拿出来。” “然后把它放进那个英俊的家伙里，否则你会后悔的。”接着，狐狸又伸出了它的尾巴，年轻人坐了下去，他们便翻山越岭地飞驰而去，头发在风中呼呼作响。

paragraphs.en: Before the castle gate all was as the fox had said: so the son went in and found the chamber where the golden bird hung in a wooden cage, and below stood the golden cage, and the three golden apples that had been lost were lying close by it. Then thought he to himself, ‘It will be a very droll thing to bring away such a fine bird in this shabby cage’; so he opened the door and took hold of it and put it into the golden cage. But the bird set up such a loud scream that all the soldiers awoke, and they took him prisoner and carried him before the king. The next morning the court sat to judge him; and when all was heard, it sentenced him to die, unless he should bring the king the golden horse which could run as swiftly as the wind; and if he did this, he was to have the golden bird given him for his own.
paragraphs.zh: 城堡门前一切正如狐狸所说：于是儿子进去，找到了那只金鸟挂在木笼子里的房间，下面放着金笼子，那三个丢失的金苹果正躺在它旁边。他心想：“用这个破笼子带走这么好的鸟，未免太可笑了。”于是他打开门，抓住金鸟，把它放进金笼子里。但那只鸟发出如此响亮的尖叫，以至于所有的士兵都醒来了，他们把他抓住，带到国王面前。第二天早上，法庭开始审理此案。 他；当一切都听完了，它判处他死刑，除非他能给国王带来一匹能像风一样快跑的金马；如果他能做到这一点，他将得到一只金鸟作为自己的。

paragraphs.en: So he set out once more on his journey, sighing, and in great despair, when on a sudden his friend the fox met him, and said, ‘You see now what has happened on account of your not listening to my counsel. I will still, however, tell you how to find the golden horse, if you will do as I bid you. You must go straight on till you come to the castle where the horse stands in his stall: by his side will lie the groom fast asleep and snoring: take away the horse quietly, but be sure to put the old leathern saddle upon him, and not the golden one that is close by it.’ Then the son sat down on the fox’s tail, and away they went over stock and stone till their hair whistled in the wind.
paragraphs.zh: 于是他再次出发踏上旅程，满心叹息，极度绝望。突然间，他的朋友狐狸遇到了他，说道：“你现在看到了，因为你没有听从我的忠告，才导致了这样的结果。不过，如果按照我的吩咐去做，我仍然可以告诉你如何找到那匹金马。你必须一直往前走，直到来到那匹马所在的城堡，马正站在马厩里；在马的旁边，会有一个马夫睡得正香，鼾声不断：你要悄悄地把马牵走，但一定要给它套上那张旧皮制的马鞍，而不是旁边那副金马鞍。”这时，儿子坐了下来， 狐狸的尾巴，他们就这样翻过树桩和石头，直到他们的头发在风中呼呼作响。

paragraphs.en: All went right, and the groom lay snoring with his hand upon the golden saddle. But when the son looked at the horse, he thought it a great pity to put the leathern saddle upon it. ‘I will give him the good one,’ said he; ‘I am sure he deserves it.’ As he took up the golden saddle the groom awoke and cried out so loud, that all the guards ran in and took him prisoner, and in the morning he was again brought before the court to be judged, and was sentenced to die. But it was agreed, that, if he could bring thither the beautiful princess, he should live, and have the bird and the horse given him for his own.
paragraphs.zh: 一切顺利，新郎躺在那里打鼾，手放在金马鞍上。但当儿子看到那匹马时，他觉得把皮马鞍放在它身上太可惜了。“我要给他好的那个，”他说，“我确信它配得上。”当他拿起金马鞍时，新郎醒来了，大声喊叫，惊动了所有卫兵，他们冲进来把他抓了起来。第二天早上，他再次被带到法庭接受审判，并被判处死刑。但人们达成协议，如果他能带来那位美丽的公主，他就可以活命，并且得到那只鸟和那匹马。 为了他自己。

paragraphs.en: Then he went his way very sorrowful; but the old fox came and said, ‘Why did not you listen to me? If you had, you would have carried away both the bird and the horse; yet will I once more give you counsel. Go straight on, and in the evening you will arrive at a castle. At twelve o’clock at night the princess goes to the bathing-house: go up to her and give her a kiss, and she will let you lead her away; but take care you do not suffer her to go and take leave of her father and mother.’ Then the fox stretched out his tail, and so away they went over stock and stone till their hair whistled again.
paragraphs.zh: 于是他悲伤地离开了；但那只老狐狸走了过来，说：“你为什么不听我的劝告呢？如果你听了，你就能同时得到那只鸟和那匹马。不过，我再给你一次忠告。直接往前走，到了晚上你就会到达一座城堡。午夜时分，公主会去浴室：你去向她要一个吻，她就会让你带走她；但你要小心，别让她去向父母告别。”接着，狐狸伸展了他的尾巴，他们便翻山越岭地奔跑起来，连头发都呼呼作响。 再次。

paragraphs.en: As they came to the castle, all was as the fox had said, and at twelve o’clock the young man met the princess going to the bath and gave her the kiss, and she agreed to run away with him, but begged with many tears that he would let her take leave of her father. At first he refused, but she wept still more and more, and fell at his feet, till at last he consented; but the moment she came to her father’s house the guards awoke and he was taken prisoner again.
paragraphs.zh: 当他们来到城堡时，一切都正如狐狸所说的一样。到了12点，年轻人遇见了要去洗澡的公主，并给了她一个吻，她同意和他一起逃走，但哭着恳求他让她先向父亲告别。起初他拒绝了，但她哭得更厉害，跪倒在了他的脚下，最后他终于同意了。然而她一来到父亲的家中，守卫就醒来了，他再次被俘。

paragraphs.en: Then he was brought before the king, and the king said, ‘You shall never have my daughter unless in eight days you dig away the hill that stops the view from my window.’ Now this hill was so big that the whole world could not take it away: and when he had worked for seven days, and had done very little, the fox came and said. ‘Lie down and go to sleep; I will work for you.’ And in the morning he awoke and the hill was gone; so he went merrily to the king, and told him that now that it was removed he must give him the princess.
paragraphs.zh: 于是他被带到国王面前，国王说：“除非你在八天内挖走挡住我窗外景色的那座山，否则你永远得不到我的女儿。”而这座山是如此之大，整个世界都无法把它移走。当他工作了七天，却只做了很少的工作时，狐狸来了，说：“你躺下睡觉吧，我来替你做。”到了早上，他醒来时，那座山已经不见了。于是他高高兴兴地去见国王，告诉国王山已经移走，现在他必须把公主给他。

paragraphs.en: Then the king was obliged to keep his word, and away went the young man and the princess; and the fox came and said to him, ‘We will have all three, the princess, the horse, and the bird.’ ‘Ah!’ said the young man, ‘that would be a great thing, but how can you contrive it?’
paragraphs.zh: 于是国王不得不遵守他的承诺，年轻人和公主便动身离开了；狐狸走过来对他说：“我们三个都要，公主、马和鸟。”“啊！”年轻人说，“那将是一件了不起的事，但你打算怎么做到呢？”

paragraphs.en: ‘If you will only listen,’ said the fox, ‘it can be done. When you come to the king, and he asks for the beautiful princess, you must say, “Here she is!” Then he will be very joyful; and you will mount the golden horse that they are to give you, and put out your hand to take leave of them; but shake hands with the princess last. Then lift her quickly on to the horse behind you; clap your spurs to his side, and gallop away as fast as you can.’
paragraphs.zh: “只要你愿意听我说，”狐狸说，“这可以做到。当你来到国王那里，他要美丽的公主时，你必须说：‘她在这里！’然后他会非常高兴；你将骑上他们要给你的金马，伸手向他们告别；但最后再和公主握手。然后迅速把她抱上你身后的马，猛踢马肚子，尽可能快地跑开。”

paragraphs.en: All went right: then the fox said, ‘When you come to the castle where the bird is, I will stay with the princess at the door, and you will ride in and speak to the king; and when he sees that it is the right horse, he will bring out the bird; but you must sit still, and say that you want to look at it, to see whether it is the true golden bird; and when you get it into your hand, ride away.’
paragraphs.zh: 一切都很顺利：然后狐狸说：“当你来到那只鸟所在的城堡时，我会在门口陪着公主，你则骑马进去和国王说话；当国王看到是正确的马时，他会把鸟带出来；但你必须坐在马上，说你想看看它，以确定是否是真正的金鸟；当你拿到它时，就骑马离开。”

paragraphs.en: This, too, happened as the fox said; they carried off the bird, the princess mounted again, and they rode on to a great wood. Then the fox came, and said, ‘Pray kill me, and cut off my head and my feet.’ But the young man refused to do it: so the fox said, ‘I will at any rate give you good counsel: beware of two things; ransom no one from the gallows, and sit down by the side of no river.’ Then away he went. ‘Well,’ thought the young man, ‘it is no hard matter to keep that advice.’
paragraphs.zh: 狐狸所说的一切都发生了；他们把鸟带走了，公主再次骑上马，他们继续前行，来到一片大树林。这时，狐狸又来了，说：“请杀了我，砍下我的头和脚。”但年轻人拒绝这么做。于是狐狸说：“我至少要给你一个忠告：要提防两件事，不要营救被绞死的人，也不要坐在河岸边。”然后狐狸离开了。“好吧，”年轻人心想，“这建议很容易遵守。”

paragraphs.en: He rode on with the princess, till at last he came to the village where he had left his two brothers. And there he heard a great noise and uproar; and when he asked what was the matter, the people said, ‘Two men are going to be hanged.’ As he came nearer, he saw that the two men were his brothers, who had turned robbers; so he said, ‘Cannot they in any way be saved?’ But the people said ‘No,’ unless he would bestow all his money upon the rascals and buy their liberty. Then he did not stay to think about the matter, but paid what was asked, and his brothers were given up, and went on with him towards their home.
paragraphs.zh: 他带着公主继续前行，最终来到了他离开两个兄弟的村庄。在那里，他听到一阵喧闹声，便问人们发生了什么事，人们回答说：“有两个人要被处死。”当他走近时，他发现那两个人正是他的兄弟，他们已经变成了强盗。于是他说：“他们难道不能被救下来吗？”但人们说：“除非你把所有的钱都送给那些恶棍，买下他们的自由，否则不行。”于是他没有多想，立刻付了钱，他的兄弟们被释放了，然后和他一起离开了。 朝他们家的方向。

paragraphs.en: And as they came to the wood where the fox first met them, it was so cool and pleasant that the two brothers said, ‘Let us sit down by the side of the river, and rest a while, to eat and drink.’ So he said, ‘Yes,’ and forgot the fox’s counsel, and sat down on the side of the river; and while he suspected nothing, they came behind, and threw him down the bank, and took the princess, the horse, and the bird, and went home to the king their master, and said. ‘All this have we won by our labour.’ Then there was great rejoicing made; but the horse would not eat, the bird would not sing, and the princess wept.
paragraphs.zh: 当他们来到狐狸第一次遇见他们的那片树林时，那里非常凉爽宜人，两个兄弟说：“我们坐在河边休息一会儿，吃点东西喝点水吧。”于是他说：“好的。”他忘记了狐狸的忠告，坐在了河边；而他毫无察觉的时候，他们从后面把他推下了河岸，抢走了公主、马和鸟，然后回到国王主人那里，说：“我们靠自己的努力赢得了这一切。”于是大家非常高兴；但马不肯吃，鸟也不唱歌，而 公主哭了。

paragraphs.en: The youngest son fell to the bottom of the river’s bed: luckily it was nearly dry, but his bones were almost broken, and the bank was so steep that he could find no way to get out. Then the old fox came once more, and scolded him for not following his advice; otherwise no evil would have befallen him: ‘Yet,’ said he, ‘I cannot leave you here, so lay hold of my tail and hold fast.’ Then he pulled him out of the river, and said to him, as he got upon the bank, ‘Your brothers have set watch to kill you, if they find you in the kingdom.’ So he dressed himself as a poor man, and came secretly to the king’s court, and was scarcely within the doors when the horse began to eat, and the bird to sing, and the princess left off weeping. Then he went to the king, and told him all his brothers’ roguery; and they were seized and punished, and he had the princess given to him again; and after the king’s death he was heir to his kingdom.
paragraphs.zh: 小儿子掉到了河底：幸好河水几乎干涸，但他的骨头几乎都摔断了，而且河岸非常陡峭，他找不到出去的办法。这时，老狐狸再次出现，责备他没有听从自己的建议；否则他不会遭遇不幸：“不过，”他说，“我不能把你丢在这里，你抓住我的尾巴，抓紧了。”然后他把小儿子从河里拉了上来，当小儿子爬到岸上时，老狐狸对他说：“你的哥哥们已经派人守在那里，如果他们发现你还在这个王国，就要杀掉你。”于是，他穿上一个穷人的衣服，秘密地来到了…… 国王的宫廷，他刚跨进门，那匹马就开始吃东西，那只鸟开始唱歌，公主也停止了哭泣。于是他去见国王，把他的兄弟们所做的恶行全都告诉了国王；他们被抓住并受到了惩罚，他又重新得到了公主；国王死后，他继承了王位。

paragraphs.en: A long while after, he went to walk one day in the wood, and the old fox met him, and besought him with tears in his eyes to kill him, and cut off his head and feet. And at last he did so, and in a moment the fox was changed into a man, and turned out to be the brother of the princess, who had been lost a great many many years.
paragraphs.zh: 过了很久之后，有一天他去树林里散步，那只老狐狸遇见了他，并且眼中含着泪恳求他杀死自己，砍下它的头和脚。最后，他照做了，瞬间那只狐狸变成了一位男子，原来他是公主的哥哥，多年前就已经失踪了。

paragraphs.en: HANS IN LUCK
paragraphs.zh: 汉斯的好运

paragraphs.en: Some men are born to good luck: all they do or try to do comes right--all that falls to them is so much gain--all their geese are swans--all their cards are trumps--toss them which way you will, they will always, like poor puss, alight upon their legs, and only move on so much the faster. The world may very likely not always think of them as they think of themselves, but what care they for the world? what can it know about the matter?
paragraphs.zh: 有些人天生就有好运气：他们所做的一切或试图做的事情都会成功——他们所得到的一切都是收益——他们所有的鹅都是天鹅——他们手中的牌总是王牌——无论怎么抛掷他们，他们总会像可怜的小猫一样，最终稳稳地落在腿上，并且因此走得更快。世人可能并不总是像他们自己那样看待他们，但他们又何必在意世人呢？世人又怎么能了解其中的真相呢？
